scope: Proposition 9.7 (Exterior beam approximation) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 105. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed base-order buffer Nb, every prescribed inverse accuracy M1, and sufficiently high finite phase and amplitude orders, there is a real exterior perturbation hB such that ∥hB ∥CNb ≤ AT λNb+3/2 p eo(T) , reduced-wave and gauge residuals ≤ eo(T) ( AT λ−M1 p + A2 T λP0 p ) , P0 = 2Nb + 7, (E2) after enlarging Nb for the required trace and derivative buffers. Its jets match those of hp at S with linear error AT λ−M1 p eo(T). The positive exponent P0 depends only on the base orders, not on later formal accuracy. On the original initial slice its support lies in (E1), up to arbitrarily thin tube margins.
